Daberath
DAB-uh-rath
proper noun
A town on the border of Zebulun and Issachar, at the foot of Mount Tabor, afterward given to the Levites; the name is taken to mean “pasture” or, from a kindred root, “word” or “speech.”

📖 Biblical Definition

Daberath was a town at the foot of Mount Tabor, on the border of Zebulun and Issachar, named in the tracing of Zebulun’s bounds: “and goeth out to Daberath, and goeth up to Japhia” (Jos 19:12). It was afterward set apart from Issachar to the Levites as one of their dwelling-cities: “out of the tribe of Issachar, Kishon with her suburbs, Dabareh with her suburbs” (Jos 21:28). The name is taken by some to mean pasture, and by others, from a kindred root, word or speech. Both senses befit a Levitical town, for the Levites were the shepherds and teachers of Israel, appointed to feed the flock with the word of God. “For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts” (Mal 2:7). A pasture-town given to the teaching tribe preaches the ministry of the word: the people of God are fed not with the husks of man’s wisdom but with the pure milk and strong meat of the Scriptures, and the ministers of God are set among them to break that bread. Where the word is faithfully taught, the flock is fed and thrives; where it is withheld or corrupted, the people perish for lack of knowledge. Daberath, the pasture of the word, witnesses that the teaching of Scripture is the appointed food of the soul.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A Levitical town at the foot of Tabor whose name may mean “pasture” or “word”; a witness to the ministry of feeding God’s people with the Scriptures.

DABERATH, a town at the foot of Mount Tabor, on the border of Zebulun and Issachar.

It was given from Issachar to the Levites as a dwelling-city (Jos 21:28).

The name is taken to mean pasture, or word and speech.

Both senses befit a town of the teaching tribe.

It witnesses to the ministry of feeding God’s people with His word.

Jos 19:12 — "And turned from Sarid eastward toward the sunrising unto the border of Chislothtabor, and then goeth out to Daberath, and goeth up to Japhia,"

Jos 21:28 — "And out of the tribe of Issachar, Kishon with her suburbs, Dabareh with her suburbs,"

Mal 2:7 — "For the priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts."

1Pe 2:2 — "As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby :"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A Levitical town of Scripture; it recovers the ministry of the word, whereby God’s people are fed with the pure teaching of Scripture.

expand to see more

Daberath faces no postmodern redefinition. The truth its Levitical calling carries answers the famine of the word in a pulpit given over to man’s wisdom, entertainment, or therapeutic counsel, where the flock is left unfed and the people perish for lack of knowledge.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the ministry of the word. A pasture-town given to the teaching tribe reminds us that the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, feeding the flock with the pure milk of the word. Where Scripture is faithfully taught, the sheep thrive; where it is withheld, they starve.
